what: A small clock circle — a dot at the hand tip stands on the 12-hour ring matching the current time, and when you hover, another dot attaches at the hand position and then follows toward the cursor angle, returning with .5s power2.out. Pressing the hand tip (within 16px) makes the hand turn, .15s later, in the direction the time flowed to that hour (by the time difference within the same AM or PM) with .6s power2.out, and the sky switches to the new time at .2s. When held and rotated, the time changes and the sky of the whole site changes — 0~4h night, .8, .6, .4, .2 at 5, 6, 7, 8h, 9~16h day, .2, .4, .6, .8 at 17~20h, and from 21h night, blending --fx-night (0~1), while also using the photo overlay --fx-img-over (night .1) and brightness --fx-bright (night .2). Text color stages are signaled by data-sky as night, yellow (5h and 19h), and day. The clock text (time) updates every minute, and pressing reset returns to the current time.

options.[data-fx-part=hand]: Needle (rotating plate) — plate with its tip drawn at the top (12 o’clock), must be
options.[data-fx-part=follower]: Panel that rotates by cursor angle (no following if absent)
options.[data-fx-part=reset]: Button that ends the time travel
options.grab: Distance for gripping the needle tip (px), default 16
options.target: Element css that uses the sky variables, default html
options.fx:sky: Event the element emits when the time of day changes (detail.hour·night·sky)
options.hover: Size to grow to on hover (rem·px, anchored top right .45s power2.out) — original 6.3rem
options.hold: Size of the panel used to measure the angle when pressing the needle (from top right) — original 8.8rem (measured after .rotate has grown)
options.[data-fx-part=face]: Clock face that does not grow (the hand tip position is measured on this face, otherwise the element itself)

use: — Consumer-side css: body { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--kf-contrast-bg) calc(var(--fx-night, 0) * 100%), var(--kf-bg)) }
note: In the original, pressing without grabbing the needle opens Contact (via click on the consumer side). On touch, the following dot is turned off and only needle dragging is accepted — the plate is small, so it doesn’t block page scroll

from.where: shared.js header right .by-egg (original LayoutHeaderClock — bgStops·textSteps sky by time of day)
